neighbours.label: the rhyming word that ends a line of verse
fire:
The river runs beneath the hill,
And all the meadow lies so still.

I wandered through the autumn rain,
And thought of you and home again.

The candle burns, the hour is late,
And still I sit alone and wait.

Oh sailor, leave the stormy sea,
And come back home to rest with me.

The winter wind blew through the door,
And snow lay deep upon the floor.

My heart was heavy, dark with grief,
As autumn stole the final leaf.

Beneath the stars the shepherds keep
Their watch above the drowsy sheep.

The bells rang out across the town,
As evening's shadows settled down.
quiet: The river runs beneath the hill near the old mill, and the meadow is quiet today.
I walked home again through the autumn rain to buy bread before noon.
It was late when the candle burned out, so I waited in the kitchen for a while.
The sailor left the sea in 1990 and opened a small shop with me as his partner.
Snow lay on the floor near the door because the wind blew it in during the night.
Her grief made the autumn leaf on the table seem heavy and dark to her.
The shepherds keep their sheep in a pen near the farm when the stars come out.
The bells of the town rang out at noon, and people settled down for lunch.

notes: card: top peaks are line-final rhyme words in poems and hymns (wife., gloom., go,, rod,, store., die.). Near misses use the same words in prose.
